newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close fractionally lower.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close fractionally lower.

text.p: French shares closed fractionally lower following as Wall Street turned initial gains into small losses, after having spent the day in a very narrow trading range.
A record close in London did not help French shares.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed down 1.14 points or 0.05 percent at 2,151.55 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,156 from 2,159 on Friday's close.
Volume was 4.0 billion francs, of which 2.66 billion on the blue-chip shares.
Eurotunnel will requote on Tuesday after having been suspended since September 30. The company unveiled a debt deal giving banks up to 45.5 percent of the share capital.

Bank BNP closed 1.02 percent lower at 195 francs after the Le Monde newspaper said the bank would bid for soon to be privatised Credit Industriel et Commercial. The government is selling 67 percent of CIC and a tender for offers closes on Monday. The bank had no comment to Reuters on the report.
Le Monde said the bid would be without the help but with the consent of BNP's German partner Dresdner Bank.

Hotel and restaurant group Accor closed 0.9 percent lower at 660 prior to reporting a higher first half net attributable profit of 104 million francs against 29 million last year. Jean-Marc Espalioux slated to become management board chairman.
Oil group Elf Aquitaine sold its 2.9 percent stake in financial holding company Cie Financiere de Suez to Belgian holding company Electrafina for six billion Belgian francs.
Electrafina said the deal was done with Suez's blessing. Elf closed down 0.25 pct at 403, Suez was up 0.39 pct at 206.60.

Insurance group UAP closed 3.9 percent lower at 108 francs ahead of its results expected on Wednesday. Analysts expect a fall in first-half profit to 750-800 million francs from 806 million last year.
